To proceed: this is the last session in the month of Jumada al-Thani in the year 1414 AH, the session held every Thursday of the week. By the grace of Allah, we have found in it much good from the brothers who attend, and from those who listen to the recorded cassettes. This is one of the blessings of Allah the Glorified and Exalted upon everyone, without doubt.

In last week's lesson we discussed the ruling on wiping over leather socks (khuffayn) and related matters. This week we will continue with what we have been doing, the exegesis (tafsir) of the last part of the Qur'an, because it is the part most frequently recited and heard by people. We have begun the tafsir of Surat al-Tariq after completing what precedes it.

Allah the Glorified and Exalted says: ﴿By the sky and the one who comes at night. And what can make you know what is the one who comes at night? It is the piercing star.﴾ [al-Tariq 86:1–3] Here, as you see, there is an oath that Allah the Exalted swears by: the sky (al-sama'), and likewise the one who comes at night (al-tariq).

Some people may find it problematic how Allah the Glorified and Exalted swears by created things, since swearing by created things is shirk, based on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed disbelief or associated partners with Allah»[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1535) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]], and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: «Whoever is going to swear, let him swear by Allah or remain silent»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2679) and Muslim (1646), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]. Therefore it is not permissible to swear by other than Allah: not by the prophets, nor by the angels, nor by the Ka'bah, nor by the homeland, nor by anything of the created beings.

The answer to this problem is that we say: Allah the Glorified and Exalted has the right to swear by whatever He wills of His creation. His swearing by what He swears by from His creation indicates the greatness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because the greatness of the created thing points to the greatness of the Creator. Allah the Exalted has sworn by many things from His creation. Among the best I have seen who discussed this subject is Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in his book al-Tibyan fi Aqsam al-Quran (The Clarification on the Oaths of the Qur'an). It is a good book that benefits the seeker of knowledge greatly.

Here Allah the Exalted swears by the sky. The sky (al-sama') is everything above you: everything that is above you is sky. Even the cloud from which rain descends is called sky, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He sends down from the sky water, and valleys flow according to their measure﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:17]. Since the term applies to everything above you, it includes what lies between the sky and the earth, and it includes all the heavens, since they all are above you and over you.

As for His saying ﴿and the one who comes at night﴾, it is a second oath; that is, Allah has sworn by the one who comes at night. So what is the one who comes at night?

The one who comes at night is not someone who knocks on his family's door at night. Rather, Allah the Mighty and Majestic explained it by His saying ﴿the piercing star﴾. This is the one who comes at night. The word "the star" (al-najm) here may refer to all the stars, in which case the definite article (al-) is generic (lil-jins). It may also refer to a particular piercing star, that is, a bright star, meaning one of intense brightness, because it pierces the darkness with its light. Whichever is intended, these stars are among the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which show His perfect power in their movement, their arrangement, the variety of their forms, and also the variety of their benefits. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl 16:16], and He the Exalted said: ﴿And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps, and We have made them as missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk 67:5]. So they are an adornment of the sky, missiles against the devils, and signs by which one is guided.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and I send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family, his Companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

Then Allah explains the matter sworn to in His saying: ﴿There is over every soul a guardian﴾ [al-Tariq 4]. The ﴿in﴾ here is negative, meaning: "Every soul has no guardian" is not the sense; rather, the meaning is: ﴿Not every soul is without a guardian over it﴾. The ﴿lamma﴾ here carries the meaning of ﴿illa﴾ ("except"), meaning: there is no soul except that over it is a guardian from Allah. Allah, glory be to Him, explains the duty of this guardian in His saying: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar 10-12]. These guardians (al-hafazah) preserve a person's deeds for him, what is for him and what is against him, and he will find them on the Day of Resurrection as an open record, and it will be said to him: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra 14]. These guardians write down what a person does of speech and what he does of action, whether it is apparent, such as the utterances of the tongue and the deeds of the limbs, or hidden, even what is in the heart of what a person believes, for it is written down against him; due to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer to him than the jugular vein. When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left. He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready﴾ [Qaf 16-18]. This guardian preserves the deeds of the children of Adam. And there are other guardians whom Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿For him are successive [angels] before him and behind him, protecting him by the decree of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd 11].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 86, verses 5–7:

﴿So let man look at what he was created from.﴾ [At-Tariq: 5] The lam here is the lam of command, and what is meant by "looking" here is looking for lessons (nazar al-i'tibar), which is looking with insight. That is: let man reflect on what he was created from. Was he created from iron? Was he created from steel? Was he created from something hard and strong?

The answer to these questions is that he ﴿was created from a gushing fluid﴾ [At-Tariq: 6], which is the man's water. Allah the Exalted described it in other verses as a despised water, weak in its flow, unlike ordinary water that rushes forth. And Allah the Exalted described it in another verse as a nutfah, that is, a small quantity of water; this is that from which man was created. It is astonishing that man should be created from this despised water and then his heart be harder than stones, — and we seek refuge in Allah — except for the one whose heart Allah has softened to the religion of Allah.

Then He clarified that this gushing water ﴿comes forth from between the loins and the ribs﴾ [At-Tariq: 7]; from between the man's loins (sulb) and his ribs (tara'ib), the upper part of his chest. This indicates the depth of the point of emergence of this water, and that it issues from a firm (makin) place in the body. The correct view is that this description refers to the man's water. Some scholars said: ﴿comes forth from between the loins﴾ means the loins of the man and the ribs of the woman. But this contradicts the apparent wording, and the correct view is that what comes forth from between the loins and the ribs is the man's water, because Allah the Exalted described it in that way.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, He is Able to return him (to life).﴾ (8) ﴿On the Day when secrets are examined.﴾ (9) ﴿He will have no power, nor any helper.﴾ (10) [At-Tariq 86:8–10].

﴿Indeed, He﴾ means Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿is Able to return him﴾ means to return man (to life), ﴿and that will be on the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by His words: "On the Day when secrets are examined."﴾ So the One who was able to create man from this gushing, despised water is able to bring him back on the Day of Resurrection. This is an argument from the perceptible to the unseen and awaited, and it is a rational analogy (qiyas 'aqli). For a person by his intellect says: if Allah is able to create man from this despised water and give him life, then He is able to return him a second time. ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [Ar-Rum 30:27]. For this reason Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, uses the beginning (al-mabda') as proof of the return (al-ma'ad), because it is a clear and evident analogy, by which the mind passes from the one to the other swiftly and without difficulty.

Its saying: ﴿On the day when the secrets are tested﴾ means: the secrets, which are the hearts, will be examined; for the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection is according to what is in the hearts, whereas the reckoning in this world is according to what is in the limbs. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) treated the hypocrites in the same way as the Muslims, for when he was asked permission to kill them he would say: "People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905), and Muslim (2584 / 63), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him and his father).]]. So he did not kill them, although he knew that so-and-so was a hypocrite and so-and-so was a hypocrite. But action in this world is based on the outward, while on the Day of Resurrection it is based on the inward.

﴿On the day when the secrets are tested﴾, i.e., they will be tested. This is like His saying: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered forth﴾ [al-'Adiyat 9]. For this reason, O my brothers, it is incumbent upon us to give more care to the deeds of the heart than to the deeds of the limbs. The deeds of the limbs are an apparent sign, but the deeds of the heart are what the matter turns upon. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ), speaking of the Kharijites, addressed the Companions, saying: "One of you will consider his prayer insignificant in comparison with their prayer, and his fasting in comparison with their fasting." He meant that they strive hard in outward acts, but their hearts are empty, and we seek refuge in Allah. Faith does not pass beyond their throats. "They pass through Islam as an arrow passes through its game" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3610), and Muslim (1065 / 148), with the wording of Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. So, O brothers, it is incumbent upon us to attend to the hearts, to reforming them, their deeds, their beliefs and their orientations. Al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "By Allah, Abu Bakr did not surpass them through prayer or fasting, but he surpassed them through what was firmly settled in his heart of faith" [[Al-'Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (2 / 190): He mentioned it in al-Ihya' with the wording "what made you excel", and its takhrij-maker al-'Iraqi said: I have not found it as a marfu' report; it is found in al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi and Abu Ya'la from 'A'ishah, and in Ahmad ibn Mani' from Abu Bakr, both as marfu'. He said in al-Nawadir that it is a saying of Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani.]]. When faith is firmly settled in the heart, it moves a person to act; but outward action may not move a person to reform his heart. Therefore, O brothers, it is incumbent upon us to attend to our hearts, to reform them and to purify them from the defilements of shirk, innovation, spite, hatred, aversion to what Allah has sent down to His Messenger, aversion to the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), and other things from which the heart must be cleansed.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So he will have no power, nor any helper﴾ [At-Tariq 10]. That is, on the Day of Resurrection, a person will have no inherent power (quwwah dhatiyyah), and no helper, which is external power. He himself will not be able to defend himself, and no one will be able to defend him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask about one another﴾ [Al-Mu'minun 101]. In this world they ask one another and seek protection from one another, but on the Day of Resurrection there is no kinship (ansab), meaning no blood relation; kinship will not benefit, and they will not ask about one another. So we ask Allah the Exalted to set right our hearts and your hearts, and our deeds and your deeds, and to grant us of His mercy, for He is the Bestower.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: we ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to benefit us all by what He has taught us, and to make us guiding and rightly-guided people, righteous and reformers.

It is our custom to begin this session with the explanation of verses of the Book of Allah. We began with Surah An-Naba', and now we are at the end of Surah At-Tariq.

Allah, blessed and exalted, said, after mentioning the oath by the sky and the Tariq, up to His words: ﴿On the Day when secrets will be examined. Then he will have no power nor any helper.﴾ [At-Tariq 9-10], He said: ﴿By the sky which returns (rain), and by the earth which splits (for plants).﴾ [At-Tariq 11-12]. This is the second oath by the sky. The first oath was at the beginning of the surah, where He said: ﴿By the sky and the Tariq. And what can make you know what the Tariq is? It is the piercing star.﴾ [At-Tariq 1-3]. Here He said: ﴿By the sky which returns, and by the earth which splits. Indeed, this is a decisive word.﴾ [At-Tariq 11-13]. The connection between the two oaths, and Allah knows best, is that the first contains an allusion to the Tariq, which is the star, and as we know, stars are hurled at the devils who eavesdrop; and in the hurling of the devils with them there is a preservation of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for here, He swore by the sky which returns that this Qur'an is a decisive word; He swore that the Qur'an is a decisive word. So the connection of the first oath is that it alludes to that by which this Qur'an is preserved at the time of its revelation, and in the second oath there is an allusion to the fact that the Qur'an is life, because He said: ﴿By the sky which returns.﴾ Ar-raj' (الرجع) is the rain; it is called raj' because it returns and recurs. And it is known that by rain the earth has life.

﴿And by the earth which splits﴾: ash-sad' (الصدع) is the splitting, meaning the cracking for the emergence of plants from it. So He swore by the rain, which is the cause of the emergence of plants, and by the cracking from which plants emerge, and all of this is an allusion to the life of the earth after its death, and the Qur'an, by it, is the life of hearts after their death, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command.﴾ [Ash-Shura 52]. So Allah named the Qur'an a "spirit" because hearts live by it.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿By the sky which returns﴾, i.e., possessing rain.

﴿And by the earth which splits﴾, i.e., possessing splitting for the emergence of plants from it.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

So the connection of the first oath is that it alludes to that by which this Qur'an is preserved at the time of its revelation, and in the second oath there is an allusion to the fact that the Qur'an is life, because He said: ﴿By the sky which returns.﴾ Ar-raj' (الرجع) is the rain; it is called raj' because it returns and recurs. And it is known that by rain the earth has life.

﴿And by the earth which splits﴾: ash-sad' (الصدع) is the splitting, meaning the cracking for the emergence of plants from it. So He swore by the rain, which is the cause of the emergence of plants, and by the cracking from which plants emerge, and all of this is an allusion to the life of the earth after its death, and the Qur'an, by it, is the life of hearts after their death, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command.﴾ [Ash-Shura 52]. So Allah named the Qur'an a "spirit" because hearts live by it.

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿By the sky which returns﴾, i.e., possessing rain.

﴿And by the earth which splits﴾, i.e., possessing splitting for the emergence of plants from it.

Verse 13: ﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾ [At-Tariq 13]. That is, the Qur'an. Allah described it as a word from the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is He who spoke it and conveyed it to Jibril, then Jibril brought it down upon the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah has attributed the Qur'an as speech to Jibril and to Muhammad, may the peace of Allah be upon them both. In the first, He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger, [who is] possessed of power, with esteem near the Owner of the Throne, obeyed and trustworthy﴾ [At-Takwir 19-21]. And in the second, attributing it to the Messenger (ﷺ), He says: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger. And it is not the word of a poet; little do you believe﴾ [Al-Haqqah 40-41]. In the first he attributed the word to Jibril because he conveyed it from Allah to Muhammad (ﷺ), and in the second he attributed it to Muhammad because he conveyed it to the people. Otherwise, the one who originally spoke it is Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

﴿Indeed, it is a decisive word﴾: "decisive" (faṣl) distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between the righteous (al-muttaqun) and the wrongdoers (al-zalimun). Moreover, it is "decisive," meaning it cuts off everyone who opposes it and is hostile to it. For this reason we find that when the Muslims struggled against the disbelievers with the Qur'an, they prevailed over the disbelievers, cut off their roots, and judgment was rendered between them and their enemies. When they turned away from the Qur'an, they were defeated and humiliated in proportion to their distance from it. Whenever a person moves away from the Book of Allah, honour recedes from him and victory distances itself from him, until he returns to the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

He said: ﴿And it is not a jest﴾ [At-Tariq 14]. That is: it is not play, idle sport, or vain talk, but rather it is truth. All its words are true, its reports are truthful, its rulings are just, and its recitation is a reward. If a person recites it at all times, he does not tire of it. When he recites it with reflection and contemplation, Allah opens to him meanings that he did not have before. This is something observed: read the Qur'an and reflect upon it, and every time you read and reflect, there arise in you meanings that did not arise before. All of this is because it is a decisive word (fasl) and not a jest. But the vain speech of people, every time you repeat it, you become weary of it, you dislike it, and you tire of it. As for the Book of Allah, that is not so.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot.﴾ [al-Tariq 15] ﴿They﴾ means the disbelievers who denied the Messenger ﷺ. ﴿They are plotting a plot﴾ means a great plot. They plotted against the Messenger ﷺ and against those who followed him. Consider what they did to the believers during their time in Makkah: torture, reproach, and expulsion. The Muslims migrated twice to Abyssinia, and then migrated to Madinah. All of this was a flight with their religion away from these criminals who harmed them with every kind of scheme. The greatest of what they did to the Prophet ﷺ was at the time of the Hijrah, when their chiefs and nobles gathered to consult on what to do about Muhammad. Whenever they proposed an opinion, they rejected it, saying: "This will not do." Then, as history reports, Satan, who came in the form of a man, suggested to them: "I see that you should choose ten young men from different tribes and give each of them a sword, so that they may kill Muhammad as one man. When they have done so, his blood will be scattered among the tribes, and the Banu Hashim will not be able to take revenge against all the tribes, so they will accept the blood-money." This is what they wanted. They agreed on this opinion and approved of it. Indeed, the ten young men sat waiting for the Prophet ﷺ to come out so that they could kill him. But the Prophet ﷺ went out through the door while they were sitting, and they did not see him. History reports that he began throwing dust on their heads, humiliating them, and reciting the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they cannot see.﴾ [Ya-Sin 9]

Do not be amazed at how the Prophet ﷺ went out from among them without them seeing him. Do not wonder at this. Consider the Quraysh when the Prophet ﷺ hid in the cave when he left Makkah heading for Madinah. He hid in the cave for three days so that the pursuit would ease, because the Quraysh had begun seeking him, and they offered a hundred camels for whoever brought him, and two hundred camels for whoever brought him together with Abu Bakr. This was a great reward. They stood at the cave in which the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr were. We all know that an open cave, if someone is in it, will be seen. But they did not see the Prophet ﷺ or Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked down at his feet, he would see us." He said: "Do not grieve, indeed Allah is with us. What do you think of two whose third is Allah?"[[These are two hadiths in one hadith. The first was recorded by al-Bukhari (3615) and Muslim (2009/75), from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, may Allah be pleased with him; the statement of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: "We set out after the sun had passed its zenith, and Suraqah ibn Malik pursued us. I said: 'We have been caught, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Do not grieve, indeed Allah is with us.' The second was recorded by al-Bukhari (4663) and Muslim (2381/1), from Anas who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, told me: I was with the Prophet ﷺ in the cave, and I saw the traces of the polytheists. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if one of them lifted his foot, he would see us.' He said: 'What do you think of two whose third is Allah?']] So Abu Bakr was reassured. Those people who stood at the cave did not have any deficiency in hearing, sight, or intelligence, but Allah blinded their sight to the Prophet ﷺ and his companion. So do not be amazed that he went out from among these ten young men, as the historians said, and began throwing dust on their heads, saying: ﴿And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they cannot see.﴾ [Ya-Sin 9]

Here the Mighty and Majestic says in Surat al-Tariq: ﴿Indeed, they are plotting a plot.﴾ And recite the words of Allah, the Exalted, in Surat al-Anfal: ﴿And [recall] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners.﴾ [al-Anfal 30] That is, ﴿to restrain you﴾ means to imprison you.

Then the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them respite, a little while.﴾ [At-Tariq 17]

(Mahhil) and (Amhil) have the same meaning; that is: wait with a delay, and do not wait with a long delay. ﴿Give them respite, a little while﴾ means: a little. ﴿Ruwayдan﴾ (ruwaydan) is a diminutive of (rawd) or (irwad), and what is meant by it is a small amount.

In this verse there is a threat to the Quraysh, consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ), and a promise to him of victory, and the matter came about just as Allah the Exalted had informed. The Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated away from them, and fighting took place between him and them. In the second year after the Hijrah, about twenty-four of the chiefs, leaders and foremost men of Quraysh were killed, among them their commander Abu Jahl. Then after eight years, or rather less than eight years, the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah conquering, victorious and triumphant, to the extent that he said, as is recorded in history, while he was holding the two posts ('Adatay [[The 'adatay of the door are its two wooden posts on either side.]]) of the door of the Ka'bah, with Quraysh beneath him, he said to them: «What do you think I will do with you?» – for the matter had become theirs to be decided by him, peace and blessings be upon him. «What do you think I will do with you?» They said: "A noble brother, and the son of a noble brother." He said: «I say to you what Yusuf said to his brothers:» ﴿There is no reproach upon you today; may Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾ «[Yusuf: 92]. Go, for you are the freed ones (at-Tulaqa')»[[Recorded by an-Nasa'i in as-Sunan al-Kubra (11234), and at-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar (5331), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Except for his saying: «Go, for you are the freed ones», which was recorded by at-Tabari in at-Tarikh (3/61) from the hadith of Qatadah ibn Di'amah as a mursal report.]]. He bestowed this favour upon them, peace and blessings be upon him, only because they had embraced Islam. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they cease, they will be forgiven what has already passed; but if they return, then the example of the former peoples has already gone before.﴾ [Al-Anfal 38].

This is the end of this surah of the Book of Allah the Exalted. At its close, I urge you to contemplate the Qur'an and understand its meaning. Take its meaning from the mouths of trustworthy scholars or from trustworthy books of tafsir, such as the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir, the Tafsir of Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di, and similar tafsirs whose authors you know to be trustworthy in their creed and their opinions.

We ask Allah to make us all among those who recite the Book of Allah with its true recitation, to benefit us by it, and to make it an intercessor for us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed He is over all things Able. And may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.
